sentences.text: Holdenius was a large arthrodire fish that grew to a length of about 3 meters.
A fossil specimen of Holdenius was found preserved next to a Ctenacanth fish that had been bitten in half.
A spine from a prey fish was found lodged in the braincase of a Holdenius specimen, likely causing instant death.
The genus Holdenius was described by Dunkle and Bungart in 1942.
Holdenius was a piscivore that used sharp shearing plates in its jaws to cut prey into pieces.
Because its prey was over half its size, Holdenius is inferred to have been an exceptionally aggressive predator.
Holdenius is a monospecific genus containing only one species.
Holdenius was previously classified in the family Dunkleosteidae but is now placed in the family Aspinothoracidi.
The Spanish taxonomic record lists Holdenius as belonging to the family Dunkleosteidae.
The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Holdenius as Dinichthyidae.
Holdenius lived during the Late Devonian period.
Holdenius lived between 365.2 and 358.86 million years ago during the Famennian stage.
